axes.model_access: Its own speech-model line: the site navigation on the day splits into "Models" (TTS API, official wording "purpose built for voice agents") and Creators (200+ stock voices); no third-party model picking.
axes.runtime: Web studio (murf.ai) + API (murf.ai/api, docs at murf.ai/api/docs, direct-fetched 200 same day); generation runs on Murf's cloud, no local model. Integrations on record: Canva/Google Slides/PowerPoint and more.
axes.local_files: Studio projects and audio assets live on the account side (the site navigation carries an Assets/Studio area); no locally-held data surface declared by the vendor was found — downloaded exported audio files are yours locally, but projects and voice libraries stay on Murf's cloud.
axes.background: Studio rendering and API synthesis are task-shaped; queueing/resume details not verified item by item. The Agents line (AI Receptionist/Call Center etc.) is a real-time conversational form, a different track from batch studio work.
axes.tools: Three product lines on record same-day: Agents (voice agents), API (TTS/Voice Changer/Dubbing/Translation), Creators (dubbing studio + Voice Cloning). No MCP support verified in official statements.
axes.context: The studio organizes work by project; no official statement verified for cross-session memory (say unknown when unknown).
axes.permissions: Account system (free + subscription); the cloning consent line is on record in the official FAQ — the cloning page states outright that "using voice duplication without consent can be considered illegal" and cloning a celebrity voice without permission is unethical (direct-fetched 2026-10-30); Instant vs Professional cloning tiers are on record.
axes.fit: Fits: a commercial voice platform combining dubbing studio + TTS API + voice agents, 200+ stock voices without cloning. Not a fit: a filed direct-mainland entry, picking third-party models, running models locally.
